pieces.text: This rulebook explains how Dancing Fish reads the US labelling regulations for retail packs, and adds our own house rules on top. Artwork must pass every rule marked In force before it is released to print. Where our rule is stricter than the law, our rule applies.
pieces.label: US Label and Artwork Rulebook

pieces.text: Each rule has an ID, a status, the rule itself, and a short note on why it exists. A rule marked Proposed is guidance only and must not block a release.
pieces.label: US Label and Artwork Rulebook

pieces.text: Front panel: The principal display panel, the panel a shopper sees first on the shelf.
pieces.label: Definitions

pieces.text: Mandatory text: The statement of identity, net quantity, ingredient list, allergen statement, name and place of business, storage instructions and the Nutrition Facts panel.

pieces.text: Content sheet: The approved product information for the SKU, kept by Regulatory. Artwork copy comes from it.

pieces.text: Release blocker: A rule failure that stops the artwork going to print until it is fixed.
pieces.label: Definitions

pieces.text: Needs review: A rule that needs evidence the artwork cannot show, such as a certificate or a test report. A named person decides and the decision is recorded.

pieces.label: DF-01 Approved content sheet

pieces.text: Why: Copy checked against an unapproved sheet can be wrong in a way no check will catch.
pieces.label: DF-01 Approved content sheet

pieces.text: Rule: All copy on the artwork must match the approved content sheet word for word, including ingredient order, ingredient percentages, allergen wording, claims and every nutrition value. Any difference is a release blocker until the artwork or the content sheet is corrected.
pieces.label: DF-02 Copy matches the content sheet

pieces.text: Why: The content sheet is the single source of truth. A silent difference means one of the two is wrong.

pieces.text: Rule: The common name of the food must appear on the front panel and must be the largest text on that panel.
pieces.label: DF-03 Statement of identity

pieces.text: Why: Built on 21 CFR 101.3(a), which asks for the identity to be a principal feature of the front panel, and 101.3(d), which asks for bold type in a size reasonably related to the most prominent print. "Largest text" is our stricter house test.
pieces.label: DF-03 Statement of identity

pieces.text: Rule: The net quantity must appear on the front panel, in the bottom 30% of the panel, in both metric and US units, written as "NET WT 16.9 OZ (1 LB 0.9 OZ) 480 g" with a space between each number and its unit.
pieces.label: DF-04 Net quantity

pieces.text: Why: 21 CFR 101.7(a) and (f) require the net quantity on the principal display panel, in the bottom 30% of it. Metric as well as US units is required by the Fair Packaging and Labeling Act (15 U.S.C. 1453(a)(2)). A pack of 1 lb or more but under 4 lb states ounces, then pounds and ounces in brackets (101.7(j)). The exact wording and the spacing are our house style.
pieces.label: DF-04 Net quantity

pieces.label: DF-05 Name and place of business

pieces.text: Why: 21 CFR 101.5(d) allows the street address to be left out when it is in a current city directory. We always print it, so customers and inspectors can reach us.

pieces.label: DF-09 Nutrition Facts panel

pieces.text: Why: Our reading of 21 CFR 101.9 for a carton of this size.
pieces.label: DF-09 Nutrition Facts panel

pieces.text: Rule: Every % Daily Value must be calculated from the declared amount per serving and the FDA daily value for that nutrient, and calories must agree with the declared fat, carbohydrate and protein.
pieces.label: DF-10 Daily values and calories

pieces.text: Why: 21 CFR 101.9(c)(8)(iv) and (c)(9) set the daily values, and 101.9(d)(7)(ii) sets the percent calculation, rounded to the nearest whole percent. A wrong percentage is a labelling error even when the gram amount is right.

pieces.text: Why: Artwork adapted from a European pack often keeps European elements that confuse US shoppers.

pieces.text: Rule: Major food allergens that are ingredients must be declared in a "Contains:" statement placed directly after the ingredient list. "May contain" wording is only for cross-contact and must never name an allergen that is an ingredient in the recipe.
pieces.label: DF-12 Allergen statement

pieces.text: Why: Section 403(w) of the FD&C Act (21 U.S.C. 343(w), from the Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act), with sesame added by the FASTER Act from 1 January 2023. The law lets a pack name the allergen in the ingredient list or in a "Contains" statement; requiring "Contains" is our house rule. A "may contain" warning for a real ingredient understates the risk.
pieces.label: DF-12 Allergen statement

pieces.text: Rule: "No Added Sugar", "No Sugar Added" and "Without Added Sugar" may only be used when no sugar or sugar-containing ingredient is added. Honey, coconut sugar, cane sugar, syrups and fruit juice concentrates all count as added sugars.
pieces.label: DF-13 Sugar claims

pieces.text: Why: Our reading of 21 CFR 101.60(c)(2), which bars added sugars and ingredients that contain them, such as concentrated fruit juice.
pieces.label: DF-13 Sugar claims

pieces.text: Rule: "Vegan" may only be used when the recipe contains no animal-derived ingredient and the Certified Vegan certificate is on file. Honey is animal-derived. "Vegetarian" and "vegan" must never be used as if they mean the same thing.
pieces.label: DF-14 Vegan and vegetarian

pieces.text: Why: No US regulation defines vegan, so we follow the Certified Vegan standard (vegan.org).
pieces.label: DF-14 Vegan and vegetarian

pieces.text: Rule: "Organic", "certified organic" and the USDA Organic seal may only be used when the current organic certificate for this recipe is on file with Regulatory.
pieces.label: DF-15 Organic claims

pieces.text: Why: USDA National Organic Program, 7 CFR Part 205 (labelling in 205.300 and 205.301). The certificate is evidence the artwork cannot show.
pieces.label: DF-15 Organic claims

pieces.text: Rule: The words "GMO free" are not used on any pack. The approved wording is "Non-GMO Project Verified", and only when the verification is on file.
pieces.label: DF-16 GMO wording

pieces.text: Why: FDA's voluntary labeling guidance (November 2015, revised March 2019, non-binding) recommends against "free" wording for genetic engineering because it is hard to substantiate. Version 3.1 replaced it with verified wording.
pieces.label: DF-16 GMO wording

pieces.text: Rule: Claims built on the word "high", such as "High Fiber", "High Protein" or "High-Grain", must be approved by Regulatory before use.
pieces.label: DF-17 Claims built on "high"

pieces.text: Why: "High" is a defined nutrient content claim: 21 CFR 101.54(b) allows it only when the food has 20 percent or more of the daily value per reference amount customarily consumed. With other words it can still read as one, so a person decides.
pieces.label: DF-17 Claims built on "high"

pieces.text: Rule: Mandatory text must be set at 6 pt or larger.
pieces.label: DF-18 Minimum text size

pieces.text: Why: House rule for readability. It does not replace the 1/16 inch minimum letter height in 21 CFR 101.2(c) (measured on the lowercase "o", see 101.7(h)(2)), which Regulatory checks on the printed proof.
pieces.label: DF-18 Minimum text size

pieces.text: Rule: Release files must not contain hidden text: no text covered by other artwork, on switched-off layers or outside the trim. Hidden copy must be deleted from the file, not covered.
pieces.label: DF-19 No hidden content

pieces.text: Why: Hidden copy can print if a layer or a fill moves at the printer. Added after the 2026 reprint of a carton that printed an old nutrition table.
pieces.label: DF-19 No hidden content

pieces.label: DF-20 Recycling label

pieces.text: Why: Retailer requirement for paperboard cartons.
pieces.label: DF-20 Recycling label

pieces.text: Why: Planning only (FDA proposed rule published 16 January 2025, Federal Register document 2025-00778; not yet final when checked). Do not apply until Regulatory issues version 4 of this rulebook.

rules.ref: 21 CFR 101.65(d), as amended by Federal Register document 2024-29957 (89 FR 106064, Dec. 27, 2024) 101.65(d)
rules.summary: From 25 Feb 2028 "healthy" needs a minimum food-group amount (a grain product needs 3/4 oz equivalent whole grain per reference amount) and limits on added sugars, sodium and saturated fat.
The principal display panel must carry a statement of identity (the common or usual name of the food, for example "Granola").
The statement of identity is in bold type on the front panel, in a size reasonably related to the most prominent printed matter there, and parallel to the base.
Every ingredient is listed by its common or usual name, heaviest first.
Ingredients are named specifically (for example "walnuts", "almonds") and not by a collective name.
All required label information is in English (a foreign language may be added only if every required item is repeated in it, with some exceptions).
The label names the manufacturer, packer or distributor and gives its place of business.
The place of business shows city, State and ZIP code; the street address may be left out only if the firm is listed in a current city or telephone directory.
Net quantity is a distinct item on the principal display panel, in the bottom 30% of the panel area, in lines generally parallel to the base.
The net quantity statement must stand apart from other label information (not run in with other text).
For a package under 4 lb or 1 gal, net quantity is stated in ounces (identified as weight), with the pound equivalent in parentheses when 1 lb or more.

rules.ref: Fair Packaging and Labeling Act, 15 U.S.C. 1453(a)(2) 15 U.S.C. 1453(a)(2)
rules.summary: Net quantity must also be stated in SI metric units (grams) alongside ounces, except for random packages and foods packed at retail.
A weight statement must use the words "net weight" (for example "Net Wt. 16.9 oz").
Minimum letter height of the net quantity depends on the area of the principal display panel (tiers listed in pack_items.yaml).

"No added sugar", "without added sugar" and "no sugar added" are allowed only if no sugars or sugar-containing ingredient (jam, jelly, concentrated fruit juice) is added, sugar content is not increased by processing, and the food is labeled as not low or reduced calorie when it is not.
"Sugar free" (and "free of sugar", "no sugar", "zero sugar") needs under 0.5 g sugars per serving and per reference amount, and no added sugar ingredient; low-calorie conditions also apply.
"Gluten free" is allowed only if the food has no gluten-containing grain (or processed ingredient) and any unavoidable gluten is under 20 ppm.
"Organic" on a product needs at least 95% organic ingredients, certified production, and the name of the certifying agent on the label.
A packaged food carries the Nutrition Facts panel.
The panel carries the heading "Nutrition Facts" and is set off in a box with hairlines.
Energy is declared as Calories per serving; kilojoules may be added in parentheses but cannot replace Calories.
Sodium is declared in milligrams under the name "Sodium"; the term "salt" (EU style) does not replace it on the Nutrition Facts panel.
Percent Daily Value is shown for each nutrient with a Daily Reference Value, using the values in 101.9(c)(9); EU "reference intake" percentages do not satisfy this.
The Calories line is in bold or extra bold, at least 16 point (numbers at least 22 point).

rules.title: Approved content sheet
rules.text: Artwork may only be signed off against a content sheet whose status is Approved. If the content sheet is still Draft or In Review, Regulatory must confirm the sheet before the artwork can be released.

source.quote: Artwork may only be signed off against a content sheet whose status is Approved. If the content sheet is still Draft or In Review, Regulatory must confirm the sheet before the artwork can be released.

rules.title: Copy matches the content sheet
rules.text: All copy on the artwork must match the approved content sheet word for word, including ingredient order, ingredient percentages, allergen wording, claims and every nutrition value. Any difference is a release blocker until the artwork or the content sheet is corrected.

source.quote: All copy on the artwork must match the approved content sheet word for word, including ingredient order, ingredient percentages, allergen wording, claims and every nutrition value. Any difference is a release blocker until the artwork or the content sheet is corrected.

rules.title: Statement of identity
rules.text: The common name of the food must appear on the front panel and must be the largest text on that panel.

source.quote: The common name of the food must appear on the front panel and must be the largest text on that panel.

rules.title: Net quantity
rules.text: The net quantity must appear on the front panel, in the bottom 30% of the panel, in both metric and US units, written as "NET WT 16.9 OZ (1 LB 0.9 OZ) 480 g" with a space between each number and its unit.

source.quote: The net quantity must appear on the front panel, in the bottom 30% of the panel, in both metric and US units, written as "NET WT 16.9 OZ (1 LB 0.9 OZ) 480 g" with a space between each number and its unit.

rules.title: Name and place of business
rules.text: The back panel must state the manufacturer, packer or distributor, introduced by "Manufactured by", "Packed by" or "Distributed by", followed by the street address, city, state and ZIP code.

source.quote: The back panel must state the manufacturer, packer or distributor, introduced by "Manufactured by", "Packed by" or "Distributed by", followed by the street address, city, state and ZIP code.

rules.title: Consumer care line
rules.text: Every pack must carry a consumer care line on the back or a side panel: a US phone number or a website address.

source.quote: Every pack must carry a consumer care line on the back or a side panel: a US phone number or a website address.

rules.title: Storage instructions
rules.text: Storage instructions must appear on the back panel.

source.quote: Storage instructions must appear on the back panel.

rules.title: Date and lot code area
rules.text: When the copy sends the shopper to the base of the pack for the best-before date, the base panel must keep a clear, unprinted area of at least 40 mm by 15 mm for the date and lot code.

source.quote: When the copy sends the shopper to the base of the pack for the best-before date, the base panel must keep a clear, unprinted area of at least 40 mm by 15 mm for the date and lot code.

rules.title: Nutrition Facts panel
rules.text: The Nutrition Facts panel must sit on the back or a side panel, carry the title "Nutrition Facts", and end with the % Daily Value footnote.

source.quote: The Nutrition Facts panel must sit on the back or a side panel, carry the title "Nutrition Facts", and end with the % Daily Value footnote.

rules.title: Daily values and calories
rules.text: Every % Daily Value must be calculated from the declared amount per serving and the FDA daily value for that nutrient, and calories must agree with the declared fat, carbohydrate and protein.

source.quote: Every % Daily Value must be calculated from the declared amount per serving and the FDA daily value for that nutrient, and calories must agree with the declared fat, carbohydrate and protein.

rules.title: US English and US formats
rules.text: US packs use US English and US formats only: no EU nutrition tables, no kilojoule energy values, no Reference Intake icons and no UK spellings such as "Fibre" or "Flavouring".

source.quote: US packs use US English and US formats only: no EU nutrition tables, no kilojoule energy values, no Reference Intake icons and no UK spellings such as "Fibre" or "Flavouring".

rules.title: Allergen statement
rules.text: Major food allergens that are ingredients must be declared in a "Contains:" statement placed directly after the ingredient list. "May contain" wording is only for cross-contact and must never name an allergen that is an ingredient in the recipe.

source.quote: Major food allergens that are ingredients must be declared in a "Contains:" statement placed directly after the ingredient list. "May contain" wording is only for cross-contact and must never name an allergen that is an ingredient in the recipe.

rules.title: Sugar claims
rules.text: "No Added Sugar", "No Sugar Added" and "Without Added Sugar" may only be used when no sugar or sugar-containing ingredient is added. Honey, coconut sugar, cane sugar, syrups and fruit juice concentrates all count as added sugars.

source.quote: "No Added Sugar", "No Sugar Added" and "Without Added Sugar" may only be used when no sugar or sugar-containing ingredient is added. Honey, coconut sugar, cane sugar, syrups and fruit juice concentrates all count as added sugars.

rules.title: Vegan and vegetarian
rules.text: "Vegan" may only be used when the recipe contains no animal-derived ingredient and the Certified Vegan certificate is on file. Honey is animal-derived. "Vegetarian" and "vegan" must never be used as if they mean the same thing.

source.quote: "Vegan" may only be used when the recipe contains no animal-derived ingredient and the Certified Vegan certificate is on file. Honey is animal-derived. "Vegetarian" and "vegan" must never be used as if they mean the same thing.

rules.title: Organic claims
rules.text: "Organic", "certified organic" and the USDA Organic seal may only be used when the current organic certificate for this recipe is on file with Regulatory.

source.quote: "Organic", "certified organic" and the USDA Organic seal may only be used when the current organic certificate for this recipe is on file with Regulatory.

rules.title: GMO wording
rules.text: The words "GMO free" are not used on any pack. The approved wording is "Non-GMO Project Verified", and only when the verification is on file.

source.quote: The words "GMO free" are not used on any pack. The approved wording is "Non-GMO Project Verified", and only when the verification is on file.

rules.title: Claims built on "high"
rules.text: Claims built on the word "high", such as "High Fiber", "High Protein" or "High-Grain", must be approved by Regulatory before use.

source.quote: Claims built on the word "high", such as "High Fiber", "High Protein" or "High-Grain", must be approved by Regulatory before use.

rules.title: Minimum text size
rules.text: Mandatory text must be set at 6 pt or larger.

source.quote: Mandatory text must be set at 6 pt or larger.

rules.title: No hidden content
rules.text: Release files must not contain hidden text: no text covered by other artwork, on switched-off layers or outside the trim. Hidden copy must be deleted from the file, not covered.

source.quote: Release files must not contain hidden text: no text covered by other artwork, on switched-off layers or outside the trim. Hidden copy must be deleted from the file, not covered.

rules.title: Recycling label
rules.text: The How2Recycle label must appear on the back panel or the base panel.

source.quote: The How2Recycle label must appear on the back panel or the base panel.

rules.title: Front-of-pack nutrition box
rules.text: When FDA finalises its January 2025 proposed rule on front-of-package nutrition information, the front panel will carry a Nutrition Info box showing saturated fat, sodium and added sugars as Low, Med or High.

source.quote: When FDA finalises its January 2025 proposed rule on front-of-package nutrition information, the front panel will carry a Nutrition Info box showing saturated fat, sodium and added sugars as Low, Med or High.
